title: Sekiro: No Defeat Previews Wolf vs Gyobu Battle in New Teaser Trailer
content:
The upcoming SEKIRO: NO DEFEAT theatrical anime revealed a new teaser trailer featuring the battle between Wolf and Gyobu Masataka Oniwa. The anime will begin a three-week limited theatrical run in Japan on September 4, 2026.

The new clip shows the confrontation at the Ashina Castle Gate, with Gyobu entering the battlefield and facing Wolf. You can watch the video below.

The anime is being produced by studio Qzil.la, which is known for working with numerous AI technologies and projects. This caused a part of the audience to believe that the anime adaptation would itself utilize generative AI, which prompted an official statement from the production committee to confirm there will be ‘no generative AI’ used.

The main staff working on the anime can be seen below.

• Director: Kenichi Kutsuna

• Screenwriter: Takuya Satou

• Character Designer: Takahiro Kishida

• Deputy Director: Shunsuke Fukui

• Chief Animation Director: Kaito Moki

• Action Animation Director: Takashi Mukoda

• Art Director: Yuji Kaneko

• Color Designer: Azusa Sasaki

• Cinematographer: Keisuke Nozawa

• Editor: Yoshinori Murakami

• Sound Director: Yasushi Nagura

• Composer: Shuta Hasunuma

• Animation Production: Qzil.la

• Produced by: ARCH

The voice cast was previously announced and includes:

• Daisuke Namikawa as Wolf

• Miyuki Satou as Kuro / The Divine Heir

• Kenjiro Tsuda as Genichiro Ashina

• Jin Urayama as The Sculptor

• Shizuka Ito as Emma

• Akimitsu Takase as Hanbei

• Takaya Hashi as Owl

• Tetsuo Kanao as Isshin Ashina

The main visual for the theatrical release was previously revealed.

The official website describes the story: The time is Sengoku. Japan is fractured into many independent nations entangled in ceaseless war. At the center lies Ashina, a land of sacred earth and ancient mystery. Two decades after Sword Saint Isshin Ashina reclaimed the region in a brutal coup, a new threat emerges from within: The Interior Ministry. Desperate to protect his homeland, Isshin’s grandson Genichiro turns to forbidden powers. The only hope lies in a kidnapped boy — the Divine Heir — and his silent protector: a loyal shinobi known only as Sekiro. This is the story of a lord and his retainer — and their quest to restore balance to a nation on the edge.

title: 5 Things That Happen in Every Godzilla Movie (And Some Fans Don’t Want to Admit #1)
content:
Since his feature film debut in 1954, Godzilla has not only become the most iconic big-screen monster of all time but also one of the most malleable characters to grace the silver screen. In his more than seventy-year history, Godzilla has been reworked and redefined in a variety of different ways . One film might have the kaiju be the protector of Earth and savior of mankind, while another might instead turn him into a scourge that is eager for nothing but wanton destruction . Even still, another film might make Godzilla a concerned parent for his own child with nary a thought for what any human on Earth is even doing.

In his nearly forty years of feature films that feature Godzilla, the variety and tonal disparity are wide across the many titles. That said, even though almost every filmmaker who brings the character to life has a different idea of how to accomplish this, there are a handful of elements and details that almost always find their way into a Godzilla movie, and some of them are even present in all of them. Once you see the pattern, though, you won’t be able to unsee it, but the best part about these recurring motifs in Godzilla movies is that it doesn’t matter that they’re always there; what matters is how they’re executed.

5) Somehow Godzilla Returned

At the end of 1954’s Gojira , Dr. Daisuke Serizawa successfully defeats the beast with his Oxygen Destroyer technology, rendering the water he’s sleeping in unbreathable and turning him into a pile of bones at the bottom of the ocean. Naturally, the success of the film meant that a sequel had to be put together, with the biggest problem being….that Godzilla died in the last movie.

No matter how many times this little hiccup occurs, the next film always figures out a way to make sure that Godzilla is back and in prime fighting form. The first time that they had to figure out this problem, it was explained in a matter-of-fact way, with the characters in 1955’s Godzilla Raids Again simply shrugging and saying that this must just be another Godzilla.

Decades later in 1995’s Godzilla vs. Destoroyah , the death of the titular kaiju was even part of the plot, as the film revealed the atomic structure of his DNA was leading to his internal temperature rising and potentially setting him up to literally explode. When this comes to pass in the closing minutes of the movie, though, the radiation that erupts from Godzilla’s body is absorbed by his son, transforming him into the next iteration.

4) There’s Always Another Threat

As the mythology of Godzilla evolved, it demanded the kaiju do more than just face off against tanks and jets, with almost every new movie in the series delivering a fresh monster for him to either fight or befriend. Godzilla Raids Again contributed to this, of course, by being the first sequel but also delivering the first monster for the series that wasn’t the titular king of the monsters, giving us Anguirus.

Each movie that followed would always bring in at least one new monster, sometimes crossing over another kaiju that had already starred in their own movie, and sometimes a wholly original one. Even for the films that didn’t deliver a new kaiju, like 1965’s Invasion of Astro-Monster , it still brought the terrifying alien race the Xiliens into the fold. In fact, it’s really not until the late ’90s, with the first American remake and then Toho’s Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah: Giant Monsters All-Out Attack in 2001, that a new threat of some kind doesn’t appear in the film alongside Godzilla. The trend immediately picked back up, though, and shows no signs of stopping (thanks to the toy market, of course).

3) The First Plan Will Always Go Poorly

The threat of Godzilla, whether in the context of the movie making him a brand new beast in the world or a lingering menace for the government, always triggers an immediate response by the military. A guarantee, though, is that any kind of first encounter with Godzilla will not go the way anyone is planning for it to go.

Shin Godzilla has one of the funniest instances of this in the franchise’s history, even providing a subversion of audience expectations, as some attack helicopters go after the early form of Godzilla, only to be thwarted when civilians enter the line of fire and the monster makes a break for the ocean and escapes.

Even Godzilla Minus One has a twist on this, showing the first encounter with Godzilla on Odo Island before he’s been fully transformed by nuclear energy. In that scene, he fully chows down on a platoon of soldiers, and nothing can stop him (thanks in part to Kōichi failing to act). All this sets the stage for the rest of the movie, but continues the trend of the first plan against Godzilla going nowhere.

2) A Major Landmark Is Going Down

Godzilla destroying major landmarks has been a hallmark of the franchise since the very first film, which had a drastically different reason for doing it. As fans know, Ishiro Honda’s original Gojira was initially a meditation on the effects of nuclear arms in World War II, meaning the destruction of major buildings like the Ginza Wako clock tower was part of the film’s dramatization of the bombs.

As the movies continued, though, making sure that major landmarks appeared had more to do with giving a sense of scale for the kaiju destruction as well as bringing the story worldwide. The result means that Godzilla has not only destroyed the United Nations Headquarters but the Golden Gate Bridge and even more locations in Tokyo.

It’s hard not to believe that this detail of the Godzilla franchise was the entire reason that the American remake from Sony’s Tri-Star and director Roland Emmerich even got made. In that film alone, the Chrysler Building, Flatiron Building, and Madison Square Garden are destroyed (though, notably, by the military and not Godzilla), with the big lizard himself mostly just stomping through the city and crashing a hole in the MetLife building.

1) The Humans Are the Main Characters

The title may always have “Godzilla” in it, and watching the giant monster cause all the destruction that he does on a major scale might be one of the primary selling points, but he has never been the one with the most screen time. Of course, it’s true that Godzilla is the central focus of the larger narrative of any movie in the entire franchise, but he’s simply not the main character in any of them.

The reason for this in the early days was cost. Filming the miniature sets, creating the special effects, and putting a guy in a monster suit was expensive, while filming regular actors having dialogue on a set was much cheaper and could actually advance the plot.

Even as the films themselves build toward a big third-act battle where Godzilla takes the spotlight, it’s because the heavy lifting of the story has been shouldered by the humans who can actually speak on camera. This has been true about Godzilla since the very first movie, was true for 2014’s Legendary reboot, and will almost certainly be the case for Godzilla Minus Zero this November .

title: 'Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru!' Reveals Additional Staff, Opening Theme, First Promo
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Maro Muchi 's Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru! ( There Is Also a Hole in the Student Organization! ) manga revealed additional staff, the opening theme, and first promotional video on Saturday. The anime series is scheduled to premiere on October 4 at 12.30 a.m. on Tokyo MX, BS11, Gunma TV, and Tochigi TV.

Staff Main Animator: Kay Yu ( Make Heroine ga Oosugiru! ), Konaming, Asari Oki , mockingbird ( Seishun Buta Yarou wa Randoseru Girl no Yume wo Minai animation director), Ame Sanzashi ( Chainsaw Man Movie: Reze-hen ) Art Director: Hiromichi Itou ( Nanatsu no Taizai ) Color Design: Arisa Komatsu ( Higurashi no Naku Koro ni Gou ) Director of Photography: Junpei Takatsu ( Tatoeba Last Dungeon Mae no Mura no Shounen ga Joban no Machi de Kurasu Youna Monogatari ) Editing: Misato Takikawa ( Tamon-kun Ima Docchi!? ) Sound Director: Satoshi Motoyama ( Tonikaku Kawaii ) Music: Tomoki Kikuya ( Bocchi the Rock! )

Cast Komaro Michinoku: Miyu Tomita ( Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai? ) Tan Otori: Hiyori Kouno ( Araburu Kisetsu no Otome-domo yo. ) Hisako Kotobuki: Haruka Shiraishi ( Bokutachi wa Benkyou ga Dekinai ) Arisu Terui: Shizuka Ishigami ( Rakudai Kishi no Cavalry ) Ume Mizunoe: Shougo Sakata ( Chitose-kun wa Ramune Bin no Naka ) Satomi Hiratsuka: Yumi Uchiyama ( Mushoku Tensei: Isekai Ittara Honki Dasu )

Music group Sangatsu no Phantasia ( Mahouka Koukou no Yuutousei ) is performing the opening theme "Kaze no Naka wa Hashirukkyanai!" which was previewed in the first promotional video below.

Naoyuki Tatsuwa ( Nisekoi , Katte ni Kaizou ) is directing the anime at Passione , with Masahiro Yokotani ( Hataraku Maou-sama! , Seishun Buta Yarou wa Bunny Girl Senpai no Yume wo Minai ) handling the series composition and script. Ryou Imamura ( Oniichan wa Oshimai! , Mushoku Tensei: Isekai Ittara Honki Dasu animation director) ia designing the characters.

Muchi began drawing the school comedy manga in Weekly Shounen Magazine in April 2022. Kodansha published the 13th volume on August 17.

Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru! placed first in the Print category at the 9th Tsugi ni Kuru Manga Taisho in 2023. Passione previously produced a promotional video advertising the seventh manga volume in July 2024.

Seven Seas Entertainment licensed the manga in English on January 14 and will publish the first volume on September 8.

PV 1

title: Even the Student Council Has Its Holes! Anime Reveals Main Trailer and Opening Song, October 3 Premiere
content:
The TV anime adaptation of Even the Student Council Has Its Holes! will premiere on October 3, 2026, with the first main trailer revealing the opening theme song. Its official English title is There Is Also a Hole in the Student Organization! The anime was announced in April 2025.

The opening theme is “Kaze no Naka wa Hashirukkya Nai!” performed by Sangatsu no Phantasia. Noko and Sangatsu no Phantasia vocalist Mia wrote the lyrics, while Noko composed the song. A preview of the song can be heard in the new trailer, which you can watch below.

Naoyuki Tatsuwa is directing the anime at Passione, with Ryo Imamura handling the character designs. Masahiro Yokotani is responsible for the series composition and scripts, while Tomoki Kikuya is composing the music.

The main voice cast includes:

• Shogo Sakata as Ume Mizunoe

• Haruka Shiraishi as Hisako Kotobuki

• Miyu Tomita as Komaro Michinoku

• Hiyori Kono as Tan Otori

• Shizuka Ishigami as Arisu Terui

• Yumi Uchiyama as Satomi Hiratsuka

Even the Student Council Has Its Holes! is based on the manga by Muchimaro, which is serialized in Kodansha’s Weekly Shonen Magazine . The comedy follows Ume Mizunoe, a student who joins the student council in an attempt to improve his academic record, only to find himself surrounded by its eccentric members. Seven Seas licensed the manga in English, describing the story:

In a student council filled with weirdos, one new member is about to have a hell of a school year! Mizunoe Ume just wanted to avoid repeating a grade when he joined the student council. After all, it seemed like an easy fix to his current academic problems. But then, he met his fellow council members. Each of them is eccentric in their own way—one’s an airhead, another’s scary, one’s secretly a pervert, but all in all, they’re just really weird! Yet somehow, they’re also oddly cute and endearing. Which means Mizunoe is stuck with them and all the chaos they bring to the table. Get ready for a slice-of-life manga that’s irresistibly charming, quirky and a little bit naughty!

title: Tokyopop Licenses 2 New Manhwa for 2027 Release
content:
TOKYOPOP announced two new manhwa licenses at Anime NYC : Lily of the Valley and Magic Soup . Both titles are scheduled for release in 2027.

Lily of the Valley and Magic Soup are part of a nine-title licensing lineup announced by the publisher, which also includes seven new manga titles.

The story of Lily of the Valley by Rangrari reads:

Lily's family chose to sacrifice her freedom, but the infamous Duke Blake has set a trap to ensnare her heart instead. Lily is sent to the duke's estate like an innocent lamb for slaughter... although Lily's love already belongs to a handmaid named Anna. At the estate, an uneasiness gnaws at her mind... is there anyone in the world who truly loves her back?

Fans can read the English version of the manhwa on Tapas .

The story of Magic Soup by Kimpeacock and Tropicalarmpit reads:

To fulfill his dying mother's wish Romiard leaves his home for the Ice Castle of Larmanilla, a magician notorious for both his beauty and cruelty. Led by a bear with snowy-white fur, Romiard reaches the castle, but… the ruthless magician suddenly orders him to make a magic soup! Luckily, the soup is so delicious that the magician has a request: “Be our slave… No, I mean our castle's chef!” And so begins a winter wonderland romance between a cruel magician, who has a heart of ice, and a friendly, warm chef!

Fans can read the English version of the manhwa on Tappytoon .

Additional details on the two manhwa , including exact release dates, will be announced at a later date.

title: Tokyopop Announces 7 New Manga Licenses Including Garagarapon
content:
Tokyopop announced at Anime NYC on Friday it has licensed seven new manga. The company stated all the below titles are all scheduled for a release in 2027.

The new licenses include:

title: Fate/strange Fake TV Anime Confirms New Season
content:
Aniplex confirmed in a video on Saturday that the Fate/strange Fake television anime will get a new season. The company first announced the news at a panel for the anime at the Anime NYC event on Friday.

Aniplex had teased a "To be continued" message in a video for the anime it released after the anime's 13th episode aired in March.

The anime adapts Ryohgo Narita 's Fate/strange Fake spinoff story.

The first season debuted on January 3 at 11:30 p.m. on Tokyo MX , BS11 , Gunma TV , and Tochigi TV . The first airing was for 90 minutes, airing both the Fate/strange Fake -Whispers of Dawn- special and then the first episode of the main television anime series.

The anime was previously slated to premiere in 2025. Crunchyroll is streaming the series in North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, and CIS.

The English-subbed version of the anime's first episode debuted at the "Fate 20th Anniversary Showcase" event in November 2024. Crunchyroll debuted the anime's Japanese-dubbed version in December 2024. It began streaming the English dub of the anime in January 2026.

Fate/strange Fake -Whispers of Dawn- directors Shun Enokido ( Fate/Grand Order commercials, Flip Flappers episode director) and Takahito Sakazume ( Fate/Grand Order commercials Fate/Apocrypha episode director) directed the Fate/strange Fake anime at A-1 Pictures . Daisuke Daitō ( Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045 , More Than a Married Couple, But Not Lovers ) wrote the scripts. Yūkei Yamada ( Fate/Apocrypha ) designed the characters and was also the chief animation director, and Hiroyuki Sawano ( Attack on Titan , Mobile Suit Gundam UC ) composed the music.

SawanoHiroyuki[nZk]: Jean-Ken Johnny & TAKUMA performed the opening theme song "Provant."

The earlier Fate/strange Fake -Whispers of Dawn- anime special premiered in Japan in July 2023. The special is available on Crunchyroll with an English dub.

Narita ( Baccano! , Durarara!! ) first published the Fake/states night story as an April Fool's joke in April 1, 2008. Narita then developed the story as a Fate/strange Fake supplement for the Type-Moon Ace Vol. 2 magazine, before launching a full-fledged light novel series with illustrations by Shizuki Morii in January 2015. Kadokawa 's Dengeki Bunko imprint published the ninth light novel volume in March 2024. The 10th and final volume of the novels will ship this summer.

Morii has also been simultaneously drawing a manga adaptation.

title: 'Fate/strange Fake' New Season Announced
content:
The Fate/strange Fake stage at Anime NYC 2026 announced that a new season is in production and revealed a teaser visual (pictured) on Friday.

A-1 Pictures produced an anime special , subtitled as Whispers of Dawn aired in July 2023 at Anime Expo 2023, followed by the first season airing in Winter 2026. Crunchyroll simulcasted the anime with multiple subtitles and an English dub.

The text— Fake/states night —was originally placed as an April Fools joke on Narita's homepage, presented as a prologue and introduction to a role-playing game. The second volume of TYPE-MOON Ace reissued it as a stand-alone novel form under the title Fate/strange Fake in January 2009.

Kadokawa began publishing it through its Dengeki Bunko imprint in January 2015, featuring illustrations by Shizuki Morii ( Fate/Grand Order: Zettai Majuu Sensen Babylonia ). The ninth volume went on sale in March 2024.

Type-Moon concurrently began releasing a manga adaptation by Narita and Morii digitally under its Type-Moon Books imprint the same month as the light novel, with Kadokawa publishing the print version. The fifth volume also shipped in February 2022.

title: 3 Reasons Solo Leveling Is Far Better Than Haters Give It Credit For
content:
Even before the anime debuted in 2024, Solo Leveling was globally popular thanks to the exceptional story by Chugong. The light novel and the webtoon’s success made it possible for the anime adaptation to reach new heights of popularity. While the main story is already over, the anime still has a huge chunk of story left to adapt. The second season was released in Winter 2025, and the animation stayed silent on the sequel for over a year. Now that it’s confirmed that the anime is returning with a feature-length film , fans are all the more excited to see Jinwoo continue his journey. However, just as many fans the series has, the number of haters is nothing to be ignored.

The series is often criticized for being overrated for not having a lot of character depth, among many other things. For a series as popular as Solo Leveling , it receives just as much hate for always being in the limelight. Although it’s completely subjective to like or hate the series, it does have a few strong points that made it so popular. While Solo Leveling is far from the best series , it’s not nearly as bad as many would claim it to be.

3) Solo Leveling Isn’t Complex, And It Doesn’t Try to Be

Solo Leveling ‘s strength lies in a straightforward story with lots of action, the protagonist’s power-up, and the layers of mysteries. However, the series is a simplistic portrayal of an urban fantasy that doesn’t try to appear too deep or complex. It’s the kind of show you read or watch for fun without thinking too deeply about the state of the world and the side characters.

Many would prefer the story wouldn’t be like that, but that’s what makes it a fun read altogether. Solo Leveling is fast-paced, which is exactly what you’d expect from a story that doesn’t delve too deep into political drama. However, that doesn’t mean it completely neglects everything that’s been happening to those around Jinwoo. Instead of focusing on heavy lore, it relies on methodical progression to help Jinwoo reach the top as soon as possible.

2) The Fight Scenes Are Intense and Often Unmatched

The only quality that sets Solo Leveling apart from other series is the level of hype battles Jinwoo has fought throughout his journey. As an action series, it nails the fight choreography even in manhwa thanks to the incredible illustrations by DUBU. However, the animation elevates even further, relying on the series’ biggest strength more than anything. It’s no wonder Solo Leveling is the best when it comes to webtoon adaptations, and it’s easily the best series from A-1 Pictures studio.

The fights are a huge part of the story, and they continue to get more intense as Jinwoo keeps leveling up. Starting with ordinary dungeon monsters and B-Rank Hunters, Jinwoo eventually became powerful enough to clear an S-Rank dungeon all by himself . However, even the finale of Season 2 isn’t the peak of his powers, and there are more surprises waiting for fans in the anime.

1) Solo Leveling ‘s World-Building Is Often Overlooked

Not many fans or even haters talk about it, but Solo Leveling ‘s world-building is one of the best in the webtoon industry. The story is set in an urban fantasy world where mysterious gates showed up out of nowhere. As if that wasn’t enough, it also blends video game rules through the system, which is directly tied to the secrets of the world. While the main story itself takes place in a realistic setting, Jinwoo often travels through dimensions to power up.

Not only that, but the story keeps getting better as Jinwoo gets closer to the truth. After he uncovers the secret about the System, he also learns about the Cosmic beings and the historic world where he has been forced to take part. The story features the world through his lens and doesn’t hold back in the juxtaposition of the modern setting and the alternate fantasy realms that are directly tied to it.

title: Kodansha USA Licenses Trapped on Tape!, Announces Print Release for Hajime no Ippo: Fighting Spirit! Manga
content:
Kodansha USA Publishing announced during its panel at Anime NYC on Friday new manga releases for its Kodansha Print Club as well as one horror license. The company also announced an omnibus print release for the long-running series Hajime no Ippo: Fighting Spirit! , which Kodansha 's K MANGA service has been releasing digitally in English.

For the first time in print in English, experience the beginning of the epic sports manga that defined a generation and has sold more than 100 million copies worldwide, inspiring multiple hit anime series! Each premium paperback will include the content of 3 Japanese volumes.

The new horror license is:

This "ancient" technology sets Jun on a quest to dispel the ghosts haunting the countryside, but is this too much for one little girl, even with her new pal and trusty pup by her side? And why did her father move them to the country in the first place? New friends, old secrets, and ghostly terror combine for a languid summer horror unlike any other…!

TNSK depicts Jun's slow, quiet rural life in gorgeous detail, blending sweetness, humor, terror, and the joy of discovery with unique character designs and rich characterization. The cute art/dark content combo evokes series like Made in Abyss , and thanks to movies like The Ring and V/H/S, the very image of a video cassette conjures terrifying associations! Throw in a dash of Spirited Away , and Trapped on Tape! might just be the eerie, adorable new series you've been looking for!

New Kodansha Print Club releases include:

Turn up the steam in this sporty, high-school romcom between a sharp-tongued girl who swears she hates jocks and the single-minded, loyal karate champ who loves her. A little spicy, a little protective, Abe-kun will get you, too!

Horror, absurdity, and passionate romance abound in this life-or-death hit manga about love between a high schooler and her ghostly boyfriend.

The prodigal daughter returns to a tempest in the tea fields in this fake-marriage, found-family love story for the ages! By the illustrator of the Ossan's "LOVe" manga adaptation!
